9595.title: Test whether an existing idle capture can remain
9595.purpose: Uses the release TPS limit and the wider target-relative RPM margin. Its separate limits provide hysteresis while actual speed settles toward target.
9595.tuning: Retention uses normalized TPS <= 3 and RPM <= target + 200 RPM. The $9F17 RPM margin also governs the DFCO spark approach gate; changing it affects both consumers.

95A9.title: Count captured observations before learning
95A9.purpose: Sets the captured flag and advances the qualification counter toward its threshold. Reaching the threshold permits the separate qualified/learning state; capture alone does not instantly authorize integral learning.
95A9.tuning: The default qualification threshold is 16 captured controller observations. It is not 16 milliseconds; only admitted main-IAC calls advance this count, and DFCO can clear qualification.

95C5.title: Release idle capture and clear qualification
95C5.purpose: Clears captured/qualified state and resets its counter when the entry/retention conditions fail. It leaves the learned baseline as a separate state rather than reseeding the controller on every pedal movement.

95CB.title: Give DFCO priority and check stall recovery
95CB.purpose: While fuel cut is active, clears integral-learning qualification. It then tests the captured controller's RPM against the stall boundary, sets the stall-air request when needed and calls the common P/I and air-composition helpers before conversion.

98FA.title: Publish the selected target and stall boundary
98FA.purpose: Publishes the common RPM target, derives a zero-floored target-minus-stall-error boundary and reports the baseline high byte. A service path can enter at the boundary calculation while retaining its requested target.

9924.title: Choose immediate follower rise or retained decay
9924.purpose: Converts the capped TPS-derived demand to the internal word scale and compares it with the retained follower. Rising demand replaces the retained value; falling demand takes the configured decay path.

9932.title: Decay follower air without dropping below current demand
9932.purpose: Subtracts the configured word decay with a zero floor, then keeps whichever is greater: that decayed state or the current TPS-derived request. Publishes the resulting follower separately from learned baseline air.
9932.tuning: The released follower decay is $0080, or 0.5 internal air unit per admitted controller call. Its actual duration depends on admitted-call cadence; a slower decay can prolong the air added during idle return.

9973.title: Calculate and cap proportional air correction
9973.purpose: Subtracts deadband from the absolute error, multiplies the remaining error by Kp and applies the configured word cap. The retained direction bit determines later whether composition adds or subtracts this magnitude.
9973.tuning: The released deadband is 25 RPM. Beyond it, each remaining raw 12.5-RPM error count produces 0.25 internal P-air unit, limited to 24 units. For a 100-RPM error: 8 raw counts minus 2 deadband counts gives 6; 6*64 = 384 Q8.8 = 1.5 air units. Overspeed subtracts this amount later; underspeed adds it.

9993.title: Qualify learning and integrate upward
9993.purpose: Publishes P, then requires qualified capture, no freeze request, no startup air and no follower before learning. For underspeed it avoids the prior upper command rail, applies the upward gain and caps the baseline numerically. Overspeed instead branches to the downward integration group.
9993.tuning: Each remaining raw error count contributes 4/256 internal baseline-air unit per admitted learning update with the released Ki-up. The baseline ceiling is 180 units. Startup/follower/freeze and qualification checks can prevent an update even while P is active.

99D5.title: Integrate downward with directional anti-windup
99D5.purpose: Requires that the previous composed command is above its lower rail, forms the downward step from error and Ki-down, and subtracts it from the baseline with a zero floor. It reduces learned baseline separately from the temporary proportional subtraction.
99D5.tuning: Ki-down has the same released 4/256 scale per remaining raw error count. The separate downward gain allows asymmetric learning later, but the current guide changes no calibration.

99EE.title: Publish the learned baseline and its reporting copies
99EE.purpose: Stores an updated integral when entered through learning, then refreshes the retained/reporting copies before returning. Frozen learning can enter the return tail and report an unchanged baseline.

9A24.title: Apply signed proportional action and stall recovery
9A24.purpose: Adds P for underspeed or subtracts it with a zero floor for overspeed. Adds stall-recovery air only when requested and uses the word ceiling on overflow. These bounded contributions form the pre-follower command used by IAC-change fuel enrichment.

9A44.title: Qualify positive IAC air-command-change enrichment
9A44.purpose: Saves the current pre-follower air command and subtracts the previous one. Decreases produce zero enrichment. A positive increase qualifies only when normalized TPS is below $50A9 and its whole-unit increase is at least $50A8; neither input is measured airflow percent.
9A44.tuning: Released $50A8 is 10 whole internal-air units; $50A9 is 26 normalized TPS counts. A +10-unit change at TPS25 can enter the lookup; +9 cannot, and TPS26 cannot. The air change is calculated before follower/BARO. This matches the recorded Rev B boundary witnesses.

9A5F.title: Scale the admitted change and look up extra fuel
9A5F.purpose: Scales the positive internal-air change by the retained shifts, saturates the lookup coordinate as specified and calls the IAC-change enrichment curve at $50A2. It produces a fuel contribution from commanded air change before follower/BARO, not an extra IAC position request.

9A70.title: Publish IAC-change enrichment and add follower air
9A70.purpose: Stores the selected enrichment byte, records the pre-follower command as next call's history and adds follower air with saturation. This preserves the distinction between the air-change fuel input, follower contribution and later converted position target.
9A70.tuning: Follower air is added after the IAC-change enrichment calculation. A follower-only rise is therefore not the same input as a positive pre-follower air-command change in this fuel term.

9F66.title: Apply the admitted active-DFCO spark subtraction
9F66.purpose: Stores the retained base/coolant-derived subtraction, subtracts it from composite spark and rejoins normal timing construction at $A9E0. The active latch also selects the later DFCO spark floor when its TPS condition passes.

9F77.title: Release DFCO spark without clearing startup state
9F77.purpose: Clears the DFCO-spark latch and saved subtraction, preserves the current composite and rejoins timing construction. It deliberately leaves shared word $01F2 intact, so the cleanup does not erase the startup owner's remaining term.

DD14.title: Age and maintain retained diagnostic memory
DD14.purpose: Updates the retained diagnostic age/checksum bookkeeping and performs the selected age-based clear path. These writes protect retained fault-history integrity rather than measuring a sensor.

DD40.title: Qualify O2 inactivity under surviving conditions
DD40.purpose: Checks fault/context inhibition, fuel-cut recovery history, O2-band position, coolant/TPS and its count gate before setting the inactivity fault. It then clears the explicitly removed diagnostic owners and jumps over their retired tests.

DFCA.title: Check high-MAP plausibility and publish its fault context
DFCA.purpose: Compares raw MAP with the selected BARO/limit representation under throttle/RPM qualifications, times the implausible condition and updates its fault/summary state. This is a plausibility check, not ordinary MAP filtering or BARO learning.

E00D.title: Observe bypass/EST response for diagnostics
E00D.purpose: Under the surviving engine, phase and diagnostic gates, compares the board feedback counter with its baseline and advances the timeout observation. It updates diagnostic state without adding a normal spark-table correction.

E041.title: Qualify retained lean/rich O2 fault conditions
E041.purpose: Uses the retained filtered-O2 level, thresholds, duration counters and their separate direction state to select fault updates. This fault qualification is distinct from INT/P closed-loop correction and raw O2 activity.

E11A.title: Merge fault candidates, maintain retained history and choose the lamp
E11A.purpose: Scans the retained candidate/current masks, applies persistence and history merges, regenerates the retained checksum and chooses the final lamp request with engine/diagnostic context. Multiple entry branches share this tail; it is not guaranteed to follow every preceding sensor check.

957B.title: Test entry into idle capture
957B.purpose: Uses the tighter entry TPS limit and actual RPM relative to requested target plus the entry margin. A captured controller will instead use its separate retention limits, so entry and exit are not a single threshold.
957B.tuning: With the released defaults, entry requires normalized TPS <= 2 and actual RPM <= target + 100 RPM. Equality passes. Byte addition overflow follows the explicit capture branch. These are internal normalized TPS counts, not percent pedal travel.

FA4D.title: Abort the current ALDL transfer state
FA4D.purpose: Clears the selected descriptor/count/checksum state and restores receive control while preserving unrelated retained payload. Neighboring vector/trap entries are separately grouped; they are not an ordinary fall-through extension of abort.

AACF.title: Subtract the selected knock-related magnitude
AACF.purpose: Preserves the selected byte magnitude on the stack, subtracts it from the word command at $01EE and removes the temporary stack byte. This group applies a magnitude already selected by the preceding retard logic; the next group chooses a signed minimum-angle floor.

7FD8.title: Calculate the base running-fuel pulse
7FD8.purpose: Combines pressure-derived density, modeled charge temperature, displacement and VE to estimate the internal air quantity, then divides by requested AFR and injector-flow scaling to form the pulse basis. Each integer divide/product keeps its own truncation, saturation and rounding; the following groups apply trim and cut/enrichment policy.

8A22.title: Apply retained temperature/startup AFR biases
8A22.purpose: Applies the surviving hot/warm biases, the selected upper AFR cap and then the reference-counted additional-enrichment term before publishing the current request. The old gear-dependent warm-bias segment is NOPed; PE qualification starts at a separately grouped later entry.

8C38.title: Finish the requested AFR publication
8C38.purpose: Applies the retained rich bound and service override, publishes the requested AFR and continues to BLM selection. The deleted shared segment and optional extension call are bypassed/NOPed. A diagnostic source pointer to this value is not another AFR command producer.

A77A.title: Scale the current low-octane adaptive retard
A77A.purpose: Uses the retained adaptive state and gain to form the current low-octane retard contribution. Its separate learning routine updates that adaptive state; the following zero-D group bypasses the removed EGR term before the composite sum.

A81E.title: Apply the prepared MAT spark contribution
A81E.purpose: Selects the positive/negative load gain, scales the prepared MAT magnitude with retained truncation and adds or subtracts its effect from composite spark. The next group separately bypasses the retired idle/transient strategy.

84BC.title: Shape a short synchronous pulse
84BC.purpose: For a nonzero short pulse, adds the lookup correction and subtracts the shared bias, then compares against the synchronous minimum and selects the distinct replacement pulse when required. The async shaping option does not gate this synchronous lookup.
84BC.tuning: The lookup addition, subtractive bias, minimum comparison and replacement pulse are different controls. The minimum test occurs before the later byte-valued voltage offset. The synchronous lookup is not disabled by the async shaping option.

8548.title: Shape and strobe an asynchronous packet
8548.purpose: Conditionally applies the same short-pulse lookup/bias, with asynchronous admission and subtraction-borrow rules, then writes the packet/offset and performs the ordered board-latch strobe. Its zero/borrow behavior differs from the synchronous replacement path.
8548.tuning: The async path uses the shared short-pulse correction/bias only when its option/admission permits; a subtraction borrow selects zero here, unlike the synchronous replacement route.

7F86.title: Choose and interpolate the active VE surface
7F86.purpose: Uses normalized TPS and the coarse RPM coordinate to select the main or lower-RPM closed-throttle VE table, then interpolates its current load/RPM point. This table handoff does not require the new IAC captured-idle flag, so closed throttle and captured idle are distinct states.
7F86.tuning: The lower-RPM closed-throttle VE table is selected by TPS <= the shared $FF8B limit and coarse RPM < 72 (nominally 1800 RPM). Equality at RPM72 selects the main surface. IAC capture is not one of these tests.
